Hi Maya — thanks for sending this over and for the thoughtful questions. Putting quick answers here and looping in Priya (solutions) and Karthik (privacy) for the deeper bits.

Short answers up-front:
- Region restriction: Yes — both Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes support region-bound data residency. For Hosted we can provide region controls for data at rest and have separate tenancy options for enterprise plans.
- Retention controls: We support configurable retention at multiple scopes (model endpoint, project, and customer level). A few primitives: TTLs on stored artifacts, per-namespace retention windows, and a programmatic purge API for immediate deletion requests.
- Redaction/sanitization: Out of the box we provide field-level masking templates and a redaction pipeline that can run on-ingest (on-write) or on-export. We also support tokenization (deterministic hashing) and configurable blacklists/regex rules for custom policies.
- Deletion SLAs: For Dedicated/Private customers we offer contractable deletion windows — standard enterprise terms are 30 days for full purge verification, with options to negotiate tighter windows (7 days) for higher tiers or on-prem deployments.

Hi Maya — quick technical call-out on implementation patterns we typically recommend for clinical note ingestion: 

1) Ingest-time sanitization (recommended for high-sensitivity fields)
   - On-write redaction pipeline: configurable rules that remove or mask specific fields before writing to long-term storage.
   - Field-level templates: e.g., patient.name -> [REDACTED], patient.dob -> yyyy-mm (partial mask), patient_id -> hashed_token

2) Tokenization vs hashing
   - Deterministic hashing/tokenization is available when you need reversible mapping across systems (with customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM). For irreversible redaction we recommend one-way hashing or truncation.

3) Cache & KV eviction
   - Our inference runtime uses KV caches; we expose APIs to evict cached keys for a tenant immediately. For PHI workloads we recommend disabling long-lived KV cache sharing and setting aggressive eviction policies.

4) Auditability and verification
   - We provide deletion receipts via the purge API and an audit log export (immutable) that shows purge operations, requestor, timestamp, and affected namespaces. We can generate a verification report for compliance audits.

Attachment: redaction-sample.jsonl (example rule set) — sample rules in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcme-Redwood-redaction-playbook

If helpful, we can provide a short demo of the purge API and a walk-through of on-write redaction rules.

Hi all — adding a few compliance-level clarifications from the privacy team: 

- HIPAA/BAA: For PHI workloads we require an executed BAA. Our Private and Dedicated deployment models are compatible with HIPAA controls; Hosted customers may require a dedicated tenancy and specific contract terms.
- Cryptographic controls: Customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS / HSM) is available for tokenization keys; this ensures we do not have plaintext key access.
- Deletion verifiability: The audit log provides operational evidence of a purge, but legal/regulatory teams often request an export demonstrating absence of records. For that we provide a report that includes pre-deletion counts and post-deletion scans of namespaces (hash-based verification).
- Edge cases: Note that cached derivatives (embeddings, prompt logs) are treated as separate artifacts and must be included in purge policies. We recommend an explicit mapping table of artifacts to purge for the first 60 days.

Evelyn — can the security team provide the standard verification template we use for audits? Maya — if you have specific page/section numbers from your internal questionnaire we can annotate them directly.

Thanks,
